A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KG-construction framework, renamed from GraphJudger to GraphJudge. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including all v3 appendices. Substantial revisions and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V2 reports original KG-construction experiments on REBEL-Sub, GenWiki and SCIERC, alongside ablations, graph-judgement tests and cross-dataset evaluation.

after.justification: V3 reports original benchmark, ablation and generalization results, plus expanded graph-judgement comparisons and an appendix experiment measuring knowledge retention through multiple-choice questions.

M1.justification: V2 judges triple sentences using learned knowledge; v3 supplies paired documents during training and denoised documents during inference, changing verification into document-conditioned fact checking (Section 4.3, Algorithm 1 and Figure 8). V3 also removes the explicit repeated entity-extraction/denoising loop from the procedural description and Figure 3, although one sentence still calls denoising iterative.

E1.justification: The three source datasets and their reported KG/triple counts remain unchanged. Appendix F adds an auxiliary multiple-choice question-answering task using original documents, denoised documents and constructed KGs. Table 6 labels GenWiki as GenWiki-Hard without defining a separate population, so it does not establish a fourth dataset.

E2.justification: The main comparison changes from gpt-3.5-turbo and PiVe to GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, PiVe and KGGen. The generalization comparison also adds KGGen. Graph-judgement comparisons retain LLaMA-2-7B but replace gpt-3.5-turbo and add fine-tuned BERT, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3 and LLaMA-3 models (v3 Figures 5 and 7).

E3.justification: The extraction backbone changes from gpt-3.5-turbo to GPT-4o-mini. V2 Table II specifies four epochs, learning rate 3e-5, microbatch 4 and accumulation 32; v3 Table 5 specifies 500 steps, 3e-4, microbatch 8 and accumulation 16. V3 adds explicit recall reporting and an MCQ protocol with generated questions and four context conditions. These are reported setting changes, not controlled cross-version comparisons.

E4.justification: V3 adds a controlled MCQ analysis testing whether denoising and KG construction preserve usable knowledge, and substantially broadens the graph-judgement diagnostic. V2's one-, two- and three-round denoising sensitivity results disappear. The component ablations, semantic-similarity heatmap, generalization study and SCIERC case study remain, with some relocated to appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or run-to-run variability. V3 Table 6's lower-upper values compare no-context and original-document conditions; they are not statistical uncertainty bounds.

E6.justification: Benchmark, ablation, generalization and judge-accuracy results are extensively replaced. For example, REBEL-Sub G-BS-F1 changes from 0.5042–0.5133 across v2's iterations to 0.5796 in v3, while GenWiki changes from 0.8561–0.8588 to 0.8457. These use changed configurations and do not establish same-setting gains or losses. V3 also adds the MCQ results in Table 6.

T1.justification: The formal KG and triple-classification definitions, triple-set equations, likelihood factorization, filtering equations and BLEU/ROUGE formulas are retained in equivalent form. Indexing, equation ordering and placement change. The procedural revisions are not accompanied by new mathematical derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a hybrid extractor and fine-tuned judge addressing noise, domain knowledge and hallucinations. V3 adds an explicit claim of over 90% graph-judgement accuracy in the introduction and stops highlighting iterative denoising as a contribution. Generalization is promoted into the abstract and contribution list, but was already claimed and evaluated in v2.

C2.justification: V3 shifts the mechanism explanation from general triple plausibility toward document-consistency checking, adds a knowledge-retention interpretation and discusses accuracy/recall tradeoffs with KGGen. It introduces limitations concerning entity-level knowledge units and unreliable reference KGs, while removing v2's discussion of denoising-induced information loss. Its new cost-effectiveness argument invokes a 70B PiVe model, inconsistent with the stated Flan-T5-XXL setup.

D1.justification: V3 updates the existing training-parameter table and judge/extraction prompt templates, adds MCQ generation and answering templates, and newly specifies training on one L20 GPU with 48GB memory. It also documents skipping similar negative tail entities. These revise and extend the existing implementation information; the setting changes are separately assessed under E3.

R1.justification: V3 removes the dedicated KG-completion review, including discussion of KG-BERT, SimKGC, KG-S2S and LLaMA-MLP, while retaining KG-LLaMA as methodological inspiration. Related work now concentrates on OpenIE and KG construction, adds KGGen, and removes Grapher. New citations also support GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3 and the MCQ-retention approach, substantially changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and methodological explanations are substantially condensed and rewritten. Dataset descriptions, metric details, training settings, pseudocode and the case study move into appendices; related work is consolidated and a limitations section is added. GraphJudger and KAIT become GraphJudge and KASFT, and the title and author list are revised.

P2.justification: The architecture and denoising diagrams are redrawn, and the motivating noise example changes. The main results table gains recall columns and color-coded comparisons; diagnostic plots are reformatted and expanded. The combined prompt figure is split into separate displays, MCQ prompt figures and a results table are added, and extensive relocation accompanies the new document layout.

improvement.justification: Document-conditioned judging better aligns the method with extraction fidelity, while broader relevant baselines, explicit recall results and the MCQ retention experiment strengthen assessment of its benefits and information-loss risks. The improvement is limited by new reporting problems: the cost argument mischaracterizes the stated PiVe setup, and the SCIERC case retains identical outputs while changing their attribution from gpt-3.5-turbo to GPT-4o-mini. The stronger methodological alignment and evaluation support a modest net improvement despite these weaknesses.
